paragraphs: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yitzchak. (A tanna cited in a baraita.)

In Kiddushin 54a, the baraita reads: “R. Y. son of R. Y. said: The stones of Jerusalem that fell are subject to me’ilah—the words of Rabbi Meir,” etc. Without doubt this is a copyist’s error, and it should read: “Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yitzchak recited the teaching.” In fact, he was an amora, a student of Rabbi Yochanan. In Yoma, chapter 3, halakhah 7: “Rabbi Yishmael son of Rav Yitzchak; Rabbi Yochanan in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai.”[^1]

notes.text: The first attribution is printed אר״י בר״י. Its initials are not expanded into a new full patronymic; the earlier English “Yochanan ben Beroka” had no support in the supplied text. Hyman himself proposes changing the wording to דתני ר׳ ישמעאל בר ר׳ יצחק, treating him as a transmitter of the teaching rather than establishing him as its tanna. The parenthetic tanna label and the subsequent correction are both preserved, as is Hyman’s confidence (“without doubt”). The source distinguishes רבי יצחק in the heading from רב יצחק in the final citation. Me’ilah is the misuse of consecrated property. ר״מ and רש״בי are rendered by their customary names, Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai, without an authority identification. The abbreviated final citation is not expanded into a newly specified chain of transmission. Neither citation nor Hyman’s emendation was independently checked against a named witness.
